newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stagnant, Podravka, Kras selling.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stagnant, Podravka, Kras selling.

text.p: Croatian stocks stagnated at 1230 local (1130 GMT) on Tuesday in dwindling activity, with an abundance of small buying orders, traders said.
"There is very little trade and least of all in hotel stocks," said one trader with a large market share.
He mentioned food processor Podravka among the few issues that attracted investors. But its price was stuck in a 316-319 kuna range, with one larger package going even below that.
Chocolate maker Kras, selling at 526 kuna, and was among the few issues bucking the trend though volume remained relatively small compared to last week, the trader said.

Kras's price has jumped from around 470 kuna a week ago since the company announced a possible deal on investment with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) that might help spur its flotation.
Trade on the Zagreb Stock Exchange usually intensifies in the last hour before the 1400 (1300 GMT) close.
Sell orders at 485 kuna for fully-listed Pliva and 1,830 for Zagrebacka Banka, also failed to spur larger buying interest.
Their respective GDRs fetched $16.47 and $32.67 in London this morning.
